text:
Sasha: Hey team — urgent ask from MercuryPay POC. Procurement is blocking the PO until we provide a signed pen-test letter, SOC2 Type II attestation (redacted ok), and ISO27001 scope docs. They also want a brief CCPA/data residency statement for hosted vs dedicated. They want the pen-test letter within 48h to continue onboarding. Can we confirm what we can deliver and ETA?

Emma: Quick inventory — we can deliver: redacted SOC2 report, ISO scope doc, our standard pen-test authorization template (needs legal sign), and a vendor attestation PDF from SecuriCheck (2024). Network/architecture diagram + sanitized logs from eng are possible. Signed vendor addendum to change scope will take longer.

Liam: I can produce an architecture diagram and a sanitized topology for the POC environment. If you want staging creds for auditors I need a service account request. I’ll drop artifacts to the compliance bucket when ready. Example path:```s3://redwood-compliance/mercurypay/poc-2026/```

Olivia: @sasha_sales @emma_security I can sign our internal pen-test letter today but will need to redline one clause about external scans against prod. Proposed replacement for section 3: 'Penetration testing of production environments requires prior written approval from Redwood Inference and must be performed within scheduled audit windows; unauthorized external scans against production are not permitted.' Send the template to me and I’ll approve/sign.

Emma: Linking the current template: https://drive.redwood.com/docs/pen-test-template-v3.docx. Note — MercuryPay specifically asked for a 'signed letter from the pen-test vendor' naming scope 'Hosted API endpoints + Console'. We have SecuriCheck-2024-attestation.pdf but it doesn’t enumerate that exact scope.

Sasha: They insisted on vendor-named scope and a phrase about 'no customer data exfiltration'. Procurement said no PO until signed vendor letter or equivalent. Also they flagged pricing: they’re asking for a temporary pricing hold / POC credits if evidence not in hand by EOD. Can Sales offer credits to unblock?

Emma: We can offer an internal attestation + redlined pen-test letter signed by legal as short-term mitigation — that typically satisfies procurement for POCs. Vendor-scoped addendum request to SecuriCheck will take ~5 business days. For the pricing hold, recommend 1) small one-time POC credit or 2) accelerated invoice with conditional credit applied if they convert — need approval from finance.

Olivia: I’ll sign the internal attestation and the redlined pen-test letter provided we include the 'non-production POC only' scope language and limit liability wording to standard. I’ll avoid promising vendor scope changes. Please attach the exact phrase MercuryPay expects so I can mirror it where reasonable.

Liam: Uploading artifacts now — topology diagram, short README for auditors explaining tokenization and KV-cache redaction, and sanitized netflow. Will mark files READ-ONLY and point to the S3 paths.

compliance-bot: COMP-4821 created -> Assigned to #eng-security, priority: high, due: 2026-06-04 17:00 UTC.

Sasha: OK I’ll email MercuryPay: offer signed internal pen-test + attestation in 24h, vendor attestation pending and we can request addendum (5 business days). Ask them to accept internal attestation for POC to unblock PO. Also escalated pricing question to finance.

Emma: :thumbsup: I’ll prepare the redacted SOC2 and ISO scope PDF and place them in the bucket. Reminder: redact customer names, external IPs, and any SLA invoicing details.

Sasha: Thanks all — I’ll post the customer response here when they reply.
